source: Summary statistics parsed from hosted job logs; each raw pure sample extracted from the downloaded matching artifact and verified against its logged block median and state digest.
ratio_definition: legacy_seconds/current_seconds; greater than one favors the current generation structure. Observer times are excluded.
controlled_training_initial_state: Generation-only diagnostic: one live reincarnator is the only preferred attacker; all other initial entities are Mortal with no titan form or seeds. Initial affinities are small finite vectors and scores are 2..8. The actor output layer initially has zero weights and biases [3,-3], favoring negotiation without fixing sampled actions. Real Categorical sampling, backward and ordered Adam updates remain unchanged. No golden promotion, end-cycle transition, target replenishment or per-generation reset is added. Population may decline according to the original interaction rules. This is not a complete aeonic cycle or a production initial policy.
scope: Same-checkout structural ablation. Only the legacy generation method is replaced. Full-cycle cases preserve the existing old-reincarnator-reference behavior and do not demonstrate sustained training. Controlled cases exclude cycle transitions and are separately labelled. Every six blocks cover all process-order permutations. Same-code repeats estimate variability, not another optimization. Normal GC stays enabled. Imports, setup, warmup, state capture and teardown are excluded from pure timings. Observer timings include instrumentation and must not be used as speedups. Raw digests cover public entities/order/array identity sharing, core world fields, network weights, complete optimizer state and three RNG states; they do not claim coverage of every private manager field, console, external LLM or arbitrary trajectories. No local M1 or complete-simulation throughput claim.
raw_evidence_scope: All 864 pure timing samples are retained by OS, case, paired process block, configuration and sample order, including wall time, CPU time, actual update totals, final digest and cyclic-GC counts. Per-generation observer data is retained for current; the harness required identical per-generation checked state and RNG in legacy and same-code repeat. Repeated per-component hashes and binary model tensors are omitted.
findings: No platform showed a consistent sustained-training advantage from restoring the original generation loop across the controlled cases. Linux ratios are approximately 0.998..1.002; Windows 0.987..1.009. Same-code controls must be considered before interpreting small differences.

The existing full-cycle 1000x12 workload favors current on all three platforms, but has only 44 updates per optimizer in its first generation and no updates thereafter. It preserves the existing passed-reincarnator reference behavior and is not evidence of sustained twelve-generation training acceleration.
The existing full-cycle 200x2 and 200x12 workloads both have 15 optimizer updates: 9 then 6. The passed reincarnator is absent after the second generation; subsequent generations do not train it.

Every generation of each controlled case keeps the passed reincarnator in the population and performs positive matching actor/value updates. Its population declines under the original kill/cleanup rules; this is not a constant-population or complete-cycle throughput result.

The macOS same-code repeat varies substantially, including much larger differences than several current-versus-legacy effects. These cloud measurements do not identify thermal, scheduling, GC or sustained-frequency causes.
